translation_en: Amr ibn Abbas narrated to us; Abd al-Rahman narrated to us; Sufyan narrated to us, from Wasil, from Abu Wa’il, who said: I sat with Shaybah in this mosque. He said: Umar sat with me in this very place and said, “I intended to leave no gold or silver in it without distributing it among the Muslims.” I said, “You will not do that.” He asked, “Why?” I said, “Your two companions did not do it.” He said, “They are two men whose example is followed.”

Ali ibn Abdullah narrated to us; Sufyan narrated to us, who said: I asked al-Amash. He said: Zayd ibn Wahb narrated to us, saying: I heard Hudhayfah say: The Messenger of Allah told us: “Trustworthiness descended from heaven into the roots of people’s hearts. Then the Quran was revealed, and they read the Quran and learned from the Sunnah.”

Adam ibn Abi Iyas narrated to us; Shubah narrated to us; Amr ibn Murrah informed us, who said: I heard Murrah al-Hamdani say that Abdullah said: “The best speech is the Book of Allah, and the best guidance is the guidance of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him. The worst matters are those newly introduced. What you are promised will surely come, and you cannot escape it.”

Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to us; Fulayh narrated to us; Hilal ibn Ali narrated to us, from Ata ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah said: “All of my community will enter Paradise except those who refuse.” They said, “Messenger of Allah, who would refuse?” He said: “Whoever obeys me will enter Paradise, and whoever disobeys me has refused.”

Muhammad ibn Abadah narrated to us; Yazid informed us; Sulaym ibn Hayyan narrated to us—he was praised—; Said ibn Mina narrated to us; Aws narrated to us, or I heard Jabir ibn Abdullah say: Angels came to the Prophet while he was asleep. Some said, “He is asleep,” and others said, “His eyes sleep, but his heart is awake.” They said, “This companion of yours has an example, so give him an example.” Some again said, “He is asleep,” and others, “His eyes sleep, but his heart is awake.” They said: “His example is like that of a man who built a house, set up a banquet in it, and sent out a caller. Whoever answers the caller enters the house and eats from the banquet; whoever does not answer the caller does not enter the house or eat from the banquet.” They said, “Explain it to him so that he may understand.” Some said, “He is asleep,” and others, “His eyes sleep, but his heart is awake.” They said: “The house is Paradise, and the caller is Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him. Whoever obeys Muhammad has obeyed Allah, and whoever disobeys Muhammad has disobeyed Allah. Muhammad distinguishes people.” Qutaybah also reported it from Layth, from Khalid, from Said ibn Abi Hilal, from Jabir, who said: The Prophet came out to us.

Abu Nuaym narrated to us; Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Amash, from Ibrahim, from Hammam, from Hudhayfah, who said: “O reciters, remain upright, for you have advanced far ahead. If you turn to the right or the left, you will go far astray.”

Abu Kurayb narrated to us; Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Burayd, from Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa, from the Prophet, who said: “My example and the example of what Allah sent me with is like a man who came to some people and said, ‘My own eyes have seen the army, and I am the naked warner, so flee!’ Some of his people obeyed him, set out at night, and departed calmly, so they were saved. Another group disbelieved him and stayed where they were. The army came upon them in the morning, destroyed them, and wiped them out. That is the example of those who obey me and follow what I brought, and those who disobey me and reject the truth I brought.”

Ismail narrated to me; Ibn Wahb narrated to me, from Yunus, from Ibn Shihab. Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah ibn Utbah informed me that Abdullah ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: Uyaynah ibn Hisn ibn Hudhayfah ibn Badr arrived and stayed with his nephew al-Hurr ibn Qays ibn Hisn, one of those whom Umar kept close. The Quran reciters were Umar’s council and advisers, whether they were mature men or young. Uyaynah said to his nephew, “Nephew, do you have access to this ruler? Ask permission for me to see him.” He said, “I will ask permission for you.” Ibn Abbas said: He asked permission for Uyaynah. When he entered, Uyaynah said, “Son of al-Khattab, by Allah, you do not give us generously, and you do not judge between us justly.” Umar became angry and was about to strike him. Al-Hurr said, “Commander of the Faithful, Allah Most High said to His Prophet: ‘Accept what is easy, enjoin what is right, and turn away from the ignorant’ (7:199). This man is one of the ignorant.” By Allah, Umar did not go beyond that verse after al-Hurr recited it to him; Umar was one who strictly adhered to the Book of Allah.

Abdullah ibn Maslamah narrated to us, from Malik, from Hisham ibn Urwah, from Fatimah bint al-Mundhir, from Asma bint Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: I came to Aishah when the sun was eclipsed. The people were standing, and she was standing in prayer. I asked, “What is the matter with the people?” She pointed with her hand toward the sky and said, “Glory be to Allah.” I asked, “Is it a sign?” She nodded, “Yes.” When the Messenger of Allah finished, he praised and glorified Allah, then said: “There is nothing I had not seen that I have not now seen while standing here, including Paradise and the Fire. It has been revealed to me that you will be tested in your graves, nearly like the trial of the Dajjal. The believer—or Muslim; I do not know which Asma said—will say, ‘Muhammad came to us with clear proofs, and we responded and believed.’ It will be said to him, ‘Sleep well; we knew that you were certain.’ As for the hypocrite—or doubter; I do not know which Asma said—he will say, ‘I do not know. I heard people saying something, so I said it too.’”

Ismail narrated to me; Malik narrated to me, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-Araj, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, who said: “Leave me alone as long as I leave you alone. Those before you were destroyed because of their questions and their disagreement with their prophets. When I forbid you something, avoid it; and when I command you to do something, do as much of it as you are able.”

Abdullah ibn Yazid al-Muqri narrated to us; Said narrated to us; Uqayl narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab, from Amir ibn Sad ibn Abi Waqqas, from his father, that the Prophet said: “The Muslim who incurs the greatest wrongdoing is the one who asks about something that had not been forbidden, and then it is forbidden because of his question.”

Ishaq narrated to us; Affan informed us; Wuhayb narrated to us; Musa ibn Uqbah narrated to us. I heard Abu al-Nadr narrate from Busayr ibn Said, from Zayd ibn Thabit: The Prophet made a small chamber in the mosque out of a reed mat and prayed there for several nights, until people gathered around him. One night they no longer heard his voice and thought he had gone to sleep. Some of them began clearing their throats so he would come out to them. He said: “You continued doing what I saw you doing until I feared that it might be prescribed for you. If it were prescribed for you, you would not be able to keep it up. People, pray in your homes, for the best prayer a person performs is in his home, except for the obligatory prayer.”

Yusuf ibn Musa narrated to us; Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Burayd ibn Abi Burdah, from Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa al-Ashari, who said: The Messenger of Allah was asked about matters he disliked. When people asked him many questions, he became angry and said, “Ask me.” A man stood and asked, “Messenger of Allah, who is my father?” He said, “Your father is Hudhafah.” Another man stood and asked, “Messenger of Allah, who is my father?” He said, “Your father is Salim, the freedman of Shaybah.” When Umar saw the anger on the Messenger of Allah’s face, he said, “We repent to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.”

Musa narrated to us; Abu Awanah narrated to us; Abd al-Malik narrated to us, from Warrad, the scribe of al-Mughirah, who said: Muawiyah wrote to al-Mughirah, “Write to me what you heard from the Messenger of Allah.” He wrote back: The Prophet of Allah used to say after every prayer: “There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner. To Him belongs sovereignty and praise, and He has power over all things. O Allah, none can withhold what You give, none can give what You withhold, and no person of wealth or status can benefit himself against You.” He also wrote that the Prophet forbade idle talk and gossip, asking too many questions, wasting wealth, disobeying mothers, burying daughters alive, and refusing what is due while demanding what is not.
Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to us; Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas, who said: We were with Umar, and he said, “We were forbidden to be pretentious.”

Abu al-Yaman informed us, from Shuaib, from al-Zuhri. Mahmud narrated to me; Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us; Mamar informed us, from al-Zuhri. Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, informed me: The Prophet came out when the sun had passed its zenith and prayed the noon prayer. When he gave the greeting, he stood on the pulpit, mentioned the Hour, and said that momentous events would occur before it. Then he said: “Whoever wishes to ask about something, let him ask. By Allah, you will not ask me about anything while I am standing here without my informing you of it.” Anas said: The people wept profusely, and the Messenger of Allah repeatedly said, “Ask me.” A man stood and asked, “Messenger of Allah, where will I enter?” He said, “The Fire.” Abdullah ibn Hudhafah stood and asked, “Messenger of Allah, who is my father?” He said, “Your father is Hudhafah.” He kept saying, “Ask me, ask me.” Umar knelt and said, “We are pleased with Allah as our Lord, Islam as our religion, and Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, as our Messenger.” The Messenger of Allah fell silent when Umar said that. Then he said: “By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, Paradise and the Fire were just shown to me across the width of this wall while I was praying. I have never seen anything like today in regard to good and evil.”

Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahim narrated to us; Rawh ibn Ubadah informed us; Shubah narrated to us. Musa ibn Anas informed me, saying: I heard Anas ibn Malik say: A man asked, “Prophet of Allah, who is my father?” He replied, “Your father is so-and-so.” Then the verse was revealed: “O you who believe, do not ask about things...” (5:101).

Al-Hasan ibn Sabbah narrated to us; Shababah narrated to us; Warqa narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, who said: I heard Anas ibn Malik say that the Messenger of Allah said: “People will continue asking questions until they say, ‘This is Allah, the Creator of everything, so who created Allah?’”

Muhammad ibn Ubayd ibn Maymun narrated to us; Isa ibn Yunus narrated to us, from al-Amash, from Ibrahim, from Alqamah, from Ibn Masud, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I was with the Prophet in a cultivated area in Madinah, and he was leaning on a palm stalk. He passed by a group of Jews, and some of them said, “Ask him about the spirit.” Others said, “Do not ask him, in case he tells you something you dislike.” They came to him and said, “Abu al-Qasim, tell us about the spirit.” He stood for a while looking; I realized revelation was coming to him, so I moved away until it ended. Then he said: “They ask you about the spirit. Say: The spirit is of the command of my Lord” (17:85).

Abu Nuaym narrated to us; Sufyan narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Dinar, from Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Prophet made a gold ring, and the people made gold rings. The Prophet said: “I have made a gold ring.” Then he threw it away and said: “I will never wear it again.” The people threw away their rings.

Abdullah ibn Muhammad narrated to us; Hisham informed us; Mamar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Prophet said: “Do not fast continuously.” They said, “But you fast continuously.” He said: “I am not like you. I spend the night with my Lord giving me food and drink.” They did not stop continuous fasting, so the Prophet fasted continuously with them for two days—or two nights. Then they saw the new moon, and the Prophet said: “Had the moon been delayed, I would have continued longer,” as a reprimand to them.

Umar ibn Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us; my father narrated to us; al-Amash narrated to us; Ibrahim al-Taymi narrated to me; my father narrated to me, who said: Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, addressed us from a pulpit made of bricks. A sword hung there, with a document attached to it. He said: “By Allah, we have no book to read other than the Book of Allah and what is in this document.” He unrolled it, and it contained the prescribed compensation for camel injuries. It also said: “Madinah is a sanctuary from Ayr to such-and-such a place. Whoever introduces an offense in it will incur the curse of Allah, the angels, and all people; Allah will accept from him neither an obligatory act nor a voluntary act.” It also said: “The protection granted by Muslims is one, and even the least of them may grant it. Whoever violates the protection granted to a Muslim will incur the curse of Allah, the angels, and all people; Allah will accept from him neither an obligatory act nor a voluntary act.” It also said: “Whoever gives allegiance to a people without the permission of his former patrons will incur the curse of Allah, the angels, and all people; Allah will accept from him neither an obligatory act nor a voluntary act.”

Umar ibn Hafs narrated to us; my father narrated to us; al-Amash narrated to us; Muslim narrated to us, from Masruq, who said: Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: The Prophet did something that he considered permissible, but some people avoided doing it out of piety. When the Prophet heard of that, he praised Allah and said: “What is wrong with people who avoid something I do? By Allah, I know Allah better than they do, and I fear Him more than they do.”

Muhammad ibn Muqatil narrated to us; Waki narrated to us, from Nafi ibn Umar, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, who said: The two good men, Abu Bakr and Umar, nearly perished. When the delegation of Banu Tamim came to the Prophet, one of them suggested al-Aqra ibn Habis al-Hanzali, the brother of Banu Mujashi, and the other suggested someone else. Abu Bakr said to Umar, “You only wanted to oppose me.” Umar said, “I did not intend to oppose you.” Their voices rose in the presence of the Prophet, and this verse was revealed: “O you who believe, do not raise your voices...” through the words “a great reward” (49:2). Ibn Abi Mulaykah said: Ibn al-Zubayr reported that afterward, when Umar spoke to the Prophet, he spoke as quietly as someone whispering, so the Prophet had to ask him to repeat himself. He did not mention that about Abu Bakr.

Ismail narrated to me; Malik narrated to me, from Hisham ibn Urwah, from his father, from Aishah, Mother of the Believers: During his illness, the Messenger of Allah said, “Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer.” Aishah said, “I told him, ‘When Abu Bakr stands in your place, the people will not hear him because of his weeping. Tell Umar to lead the prayer.’” He said, “Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer.” Aishah said: I told Hafsah, “Say: When Abu Bakr stands in your place, the people will not hear him because of his weeping, so tell Umar to lead the people in prayer.” Hafsah did so. The Messenger of Allah said: “You are indeed like the women who were with Joseph. Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer.” Hafsah said to Aishah, “I never get anything good from you.”

Adam narrated to us; Ibn Abi Dhib narrated to us; al-Zuhri narrated to us, from Sahl ibn Sad al-Saidi, who said: Uwaymir came to Asim ibn Adi and said, “What do you think if a man finds another man with his wife and kills him? Would you kill him for that? Asim, ask the Messenger of Allah for me.” Asim asked him, but the Prophet disliked such questions and criticized them. Asim returned and told him that the Prophet disliked questions. Uwaymir said, “By Allah, I will go to the Prophet.” He came, and Allah had revealed Quran concerning them behind Asim. The Prophet said to him, “Allah has revealed Quran concerning you.” He called the two of them, and they performed mutual imprecation. Then Uwaymir said, “I would be lying about her, Messenger of Allah, if I kept her,” so he separated from her. The Prophet had not ordered him to separate from her; thus the practice concerning spouses who invoke mutual curses was established. The Prophet said: “Look at her. If she gives birth to a short, reddish child like a lizard, I think he has lied. If she gives birth to a dark-complexioned, wide-eyed child with large buttocks, I think he has told the truth about her.” She gave birth to a child of the disliked description.
